questions.q: Why does this lab use Queueable Apex rather than Batch Apex for the nightly sync's actual work?
options: Batch Apex cannot make HTTP callouts under any circumstances
Queueable Apex is required any time Scheduled Apex is involved

The nightly volume is small and bounded, and the job needs a callout and job tracking — exactly the profile the decision framework points toward Queueable Apex for, rather than Batch Apex's large-volume use case
Batch Apex can only run once per calendar month
questions.explain: This job's nightly record volume is small and bounded (a few hundred Accounts), unlike Lesson 13's unbounded Lead cleanup — but it needs an HTTP callout and job tracking, which is exactly the shape Lesson 12's framework matches to Queueable Apex rather than Batch Apex.

questions.q: Why does AccountNightlySyncJob implement Database.AllowsCallouts in addition to Queueable?
options: Database.AllowsCallouts is required on every Queueable class regardless of what it does
Because execute makes a real HTTP callout, and Database.AllowsCallouts is required for a Queueable class to be allowed to do that
It's needed to let the job carry state across chunks
It's needed so System.enqueueJob returns a non-null job Id
questions.explain: A Queueable class that performs callouts must implement Database.AllowsCallouts, exactly as Lesson 4 covered — without it, the callout inside execute would throw a runtime error.

questions.q: What role does NightlyAccountSyncSchedule play in this design?
options: It directly performs the HTTP callouts itself, replacing the need for a Queueable job
It is a Batch Apex class that processes the Accounts in chunks
It has no functional purpose and exists only for naming clarity
It implements Schedulable and its execute method enqueues AccountNightlySyncJob, so the schedule decides when the sync runs while the Queueable job decides what work actually happens
questions.explain: NightlyAccountSyncSchedule implements Schedulable, and its execute method calls System.enqueueJob to hand the real work off to the Queueable AccountNightlySyncJob — the schedule-then-enqueue pattern this lesson teaches.

questions.q: What does leaving Needs_External_Sync__c set to true after a failed callout accomplish?
options: It permanently blocks that Account from ever being synced
It creates a simple, built-in retry: the Account stays flagged and will naturally be picked up again on the next night's scheduled run
It triggers an immediate retry within the same transaction
It has no effect, since the field is read-only after insert
questions.explain: Only clearing the flag on a confirmed successful (200) response means a failed callout leaves the Account flagged for sync, so it's automatically retried the next time the scheduled job runs — without any extra retry logic needed.

questions.q: Which query from this lesson confirms the nightly schedule actually registered, and when it will next run?
options: SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Needs_External_Sync__c = true
SELECT Status FROM AsyncApexJob WHERE JobType = 'Future'
SELECT CronJobDetail.Name, CronExpression, NextFireTime, State FROM CronTrigger WHERE CronJobDetail.Name = 'Nightly Account Sync'
SELECT COUNT(Id) FROM Lead
questions.explain: Querying CronTrigger joined to CronJobDetail by job name, selecting CronExpression, NextFireTime, and State, is the SOQL equivalent of checking the Scheduled Jobs Setup page from Lesson 9 — confirming the schedule registered and showing when it fires next.
